stem: A client reports focal right-lower-quadrant abdominal pain. When the nurse begins light palpation, which area should be palpated last?

options.A: The right lower quadrant where the client reports the greatest pain
options.B: The quadrant farthest from the pain regardless of other findings
options.C: The first quadrant auscultated for bowel sounds
options.D: The suprapubic area in every abdominal assessment

rationale: NCBI Nursing Skills instructs the nurse to palpate the area of abdominal pain last. Beginning away from the painful site allows assessment of less tender areas before discomfort or guarding is increased. Therefore the client's right lower quadrant should be palpated last in this scenario. The other options do not reflect the pain-directed palpation principle.
educational_objective: During abdominal assessment, palpate the area of greatest reported pain last.
source_organization: National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) — Open RN Nursing Skills
source_locator: Objective Assessment / Palpation instructions: if the patient reports abdominal pain, palpate that area last; palpation guidance begins away from the painful area and proceeds systematically
source_claim_supported: During abdominal palpation, the area in which the client reports pain should be assessed last.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential, Related Activity Statements, printed p.13 / PDF p.17: perform focused assessments and recognize changes in client condition
blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — focused abdominal assessment / pain-directed palpation
correction_summary: Removed a redundant second item testing the same abdominal inspect-auscultate-palpate sequence already audited in Q1217. Replaced it with the independently source-supported rule to palpate the painful abdominal area last and corrected the blueprint to focused assessment under Reduction of Risk Potential.
audit_findings: A directly matches the NCBI Nursing Skills instruction. B is not the actual rule; assessment may begin away from pain, but the clinically relevant requirement is that the most painful area be left until last. C confuses auscultation location with palpation sequence. D is an unsupported universal. The final item is distinct from Q1217, contains one best answer, and avoids unnecessary procedural precision. Blueprint mapping is supported by NCSBN 2026 focused-assessment activity statements.
